rulers.name: Zhang Lexing
rulers.title: leader of the Nian; 'Lord of the Alliance' (1856); 'Great Han Prince with the Mandate of Heaven'
rulers.note: Zhang page: 'In 1852 he was chosen to lead the Nian'; 'in 1856 was bestowed with the title Lord of the Alliance'; 'In 1863 he was defeated and captured ... by Mongol cavalry general Sengge Rinchen'. The Nian page words the end differently (see notes).

correction.text: the rebel zone: Nian groups in Henan and Anhui, 1851-1868

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Nian row. The page calls the Nian 'an insurrection against the Qing dynasty in northern China from 1851 to 1868' and places Nian groups in Henan and Anhui; it names no county, river, base or banner territory (Huaibei appears only as the origin of the word 'nian'). A ring cut to Henan and Anhui (113.5-118.5 E, 32.3-35.5 N) is the researcher's reading of 'Nian groups in Henan and Anhui' and stands for the rebel zone. The raiding of 1855-1867 (Beijing's lines cut 'by the summer' of 1855, Western Army advancing on Beijing in late 1866) moved far outside it and is not drawn. No infobox area.

region.text: Nian groups in Henan and Anhui

ledger.note: 1851: the Nian insurrection begins. Infobox and lead: 'an insurrection against the Qing dynasty in northern China from 1851 to 1868'; the movement was 'formed in the late 1840s' and by 1851 'numbered approximately 2000'. The page gives the year but no month, and names Nian groups in Henan and Anhui without a base.

region.text: most of the Nian-held land, retaken by Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang

ledger.note: late 1867: 'By late 1867' Li Hongzhang's and Zuo Zongtang's forces 'had recaptured most Nian territory' (the page gives no month). After the Western Army was defeated southwest of Beijing and the Eastern Army under Lai Wenguang stayed in central China (both after the split of late 1866). The page does not locate the remnant that held out into 1868.

region.text: the remnant of the Nian zone

ledger.note: early 1868: 'In early 1868, the remnants were crushed' by government troops and the Ever Victorious Army; infobox result Qing victory. The page gives no month and no place for the last fight.

wars.name: Nian Rebellion

zones.text: Nian groups in Henan and Anhui; the Western Army reached the approaches of Beijing in late 1866

wars.outcome: Qing victory: Sengge Rinchen was killed in late 1865 at the Battle of Goulawjai; Zeng Guofan was relieved and replaced by Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang; most Nian territory was retaken by late 1867 and 'in early 1868, the remnants were crushed'.
wars.note: Taiping commanders Lai Wenguang and Fan Ruzeng 'arrived to take control of Nian forces' in late 1864 (page), after the fall of Nanjing in July 1864 (Taiping dossier); the Nian split into an Eastern Army (Lai Wenguang) and a Western Army (Zhang Zongyu) in late 1866.

certainty.note: A decentralised insurgency: the pages name Nian groups in Henan and Anhui and the raids, but no base area, county list or banner territory, so the whole life rests on a researcher's ring.

sources.title: Nian rebellion
sources.note: Dates: 1851-1868; late 1864 Taiping commanders; late 1866 split into Eastern and Western armies; Sengge Rinchen killed late 1865; Zeng Guofan replaced by Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang; most Nian territory retaken by late 1867; remnants crushed early 1868.

sources.title: Zhang Lexing
sources.note: 1852 chosen to lead; 1856 'Lord of the Alliance' and the banner system; 1863 captured by Sengge Rinchen. Silent on his base, the 1855 assembly and the towns held.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from two pages (the Nian page is thin on territory). Not settled: (1) where the Nian held land. The Nian page names Nian groups in Henan and Anhui only; it is silent on Guoyang, the Zhi River, the Huaibei plain as a base, Shandong and Zhili, so the ring is a stand-in and the dossier is soft throughout; a gap-filler with a book could replace it. (2) Zhang Lexing's end. The Nian page has him 'killed in an ambush' in 1863 and also says Sengge Rinchen 'killed Zhang himself'; the Zhang Lexing page says he was 'defeated and captured' in 1863 and gives no execution date or place. (3) Titles: the Nian page has 'Bright King of the Great Han' with no date; the Zhang page has 'Lord of the Alliance' (1856) and 'Great Han Prince with the Mandate of Heaven' with no date. No 'Great Han Heavenly Kingdom' proclamation is on either page. (4) The Nian page's 1858 'effectively dissolved' of the five banner confederation of 1856 sits beside the movement lasting to 1868; read here as a loss of cohesion, not an end. (5) The 'late 1864' Taiping commanders' takeover is not a gain or vassal event: the page does not say land changed hands. Counterpart: qing-dynasty (written by ea-08-a/b); taiping-heavenly-kingdom is an existing dossier. Family china-division is the researcher's pick; the colour agent may move it. No Cliopatria shape is reviewed (no Nian row exists).
